Operator: Good day, and welcome to the NovaTel Communications Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question during the Q&A, press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to NovaTel Communications Inc.'s Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me on the call today are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Maria Chen, Chief Financial Officer; David Patel, Chief Network Officer; Lisa Wong, Chief Commercial Officer; Raj Singh, Chief Technology Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more complete discussion of these risks.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. We're very pleased with our performance in the Q3, driven by strong execution and a favorable market environment. We are focused on delivering long-term sustainable growth.

Our achievements include the standout results from our new product and service launches, which accelerated both revenue and subscriber momentum through our Converge5G strategy blending high-speed 5G with premium media and edge content. We are also seeing substantial growth from NovaFWA Ultra with a significant expansion in fixed wireless access and bundled streaming. Further, we are concentrating on robust free cash flow generation, which supports our capital allocation priorities. Additionally, our capital expenditure plans for network investments are on track to fuel future growth. We are also guiding for solid subscriber and revenue expansion in the coming periods. Improving subscriber acquisition costs are enhancing efficiency, while our operating expense initiatives are boosting profitability. Finally, our debt management keeps leverage at healthy levels as we deleverage steadily.

Maria Chen: Thank you, Alex. Moving to the financials, our revenue for the quarter was $15.2 billion, representing a 7% year-over-year increase. Adjusted EBITDA was $5.6 billion, resulting in a margin of 37%. We continue to manage our expenses prudently and are optimizing our capital allocation. Capital expenditures were $4.2 billion, primarily focused on expanding our 5G network and fiber infrastructure.

To expand on that, let me first highlight the exceptional impact from our new product and service launches, which have been pivotal drivers of revenue acceleration and subscriber gains this quarter. Under our Converge5G strategy, we're merging high-speed 5G networks with premium media and edge content delivery to gain share in this competitive telecom-media space. Specifically, the nationwide rollout of 5G Fixed Wireless Access via NovaFWA Ultra, bundled 5G Home Internet with ad-supported streaming on NovaStream, and low-latency 5G Ultra Wideband mobile plans integrated with Apple One and Disney+ bundles produced $1.2 billion in incremental revenue in Q3. That's a 28% jump from Q2's $935 million and accounts for 15% of our total $15.2 billion quarterly revenue. Year-over-year, these drove a 22% uplift in service revenue, well above the industry's 4-6% per Light Reading benchmarks.

NovaFWA Ultra alone generated $650 million, powered by Open RAN deployments with Nokia and Rakuten Symphony that cut capex 18% while achieving sub-10ms latency for 8K streaming and AR/VR gaming. Media bundles added $420 million, lifting ARPU by $8.50 monthly for 4.2 million early adopters—higher margins than Comcast's Xfinity due to zero-rated partner content. Enterprise edge services, including 5G Private Network slices for media production, tapped post-strike Hollywood demand for the rest.

On subscribers, we added a massive 2.8 million net adds across broadband, wireless postpaid, and video/streaming RGUs. Wireless postpaid saw 1.5 million adds, up 35% YoY, with smartphone penetration at 72% and iPhone 15 activations surging 45% via Apple One bundles featuring spatial audio and cloud gaming. Broadband gained 850,000 adds, pushing FWA subs to 3.1 million and closing in on T-Mobile's lead, with churn falling to 0.9% from 1.4% amid BEAD rural subsidies. Video/Streaming added 450,000 to NovaStream, 62% on the $15 ad-supported tier bundled with wireless, reversing cord-cutting via hybrid IPTV-OTT.

The U.S. drove 75% of adds at 2.1 million, leveraging mmWave in top 50 metros and FCC auctions. Europe added 450,000 FWA subs through our Vodafone JV in the UK and Germany under EU Gigabit mandates, though bundling regs limited it to 18% YoY. In APAC, IndiTel in India exploded with 250,000 mobile adds on ₹299 (~$3.60) plans, differentiating via Hotstar content amid Jio price wars.

This convergence boosted blended ARPU 12% to $58.20, expanding EBITDA margins 250 bps to 42% via AI network slicing and NVIDIA Edge AI for churn prediction. FWA LTV hits $4,200 over 48 months, 20% above wireless peers. We see $5.2 billion from these in FY2024, with Q4 targeting 3.2 million adds on holiday ramps and Black Friday deals. Risks include spectrum refarming and AT&T fiber, but 5G SA upgrades prep us for 6G pilots by 2026.

Shifting to free cash flow, which remains central to our strength, we generated $2.8 billion in Q3, up 18% YoY and our 11th straight quarter of growth. Trailing twelve months stand at $11.2 billion, or 12% FCF conversion from $28.4 billion adjusted EBITDA—key in our 5G densification and streaming battles.

Operating cash flow hit $4.9 billion, up 14% YoY, from 4.2% postpaid ARPU growth to $58.30 on 5G Ultra Wideband and FWA serving 2.8 million homes, up 45%. Broadband revenue rose 9% to $3.2 billion with 35 million FTTH passings via RDOF/BEAD. NexusStream—wait, NovaStream—added 1.2 million subs to 48 million, ad revenue up 22%. We freed $450 million working capital via vendor terms with Ericsson and Nokia.

Capex controlled at $2.1 billion or 22% of revenue, down from 25%, post C-band peaks. 55% or $1.15 billion to network including Open RAN pilots cutting TCO 25%; 25% CPE for FWA gateways; $350 million media CDN with Akamai/AWS for sub-2s latency on NBA/NFL.

North America: 72% of FCF at $2.0 billion via enterprise 5G for manufacturing URLLC. EMEA: $450 million up 12% with €1.2 billion RGE rural fiber. APAC: $350 million, 30% YoY on India/Indonesia 5G SA.

Utilization: 45% or $1.26 billion to shareholders—$850 million dividends at $0.65/share (2.8% yield), $410 million buybacks under $15 billion program (12 million shares YTD at $42 avg, 4% EPS accretion). 30% or $840 million debt reduction: prepaid $600 million 2026 notes, repaid $240 million revolver, net debt/EBITDA to 2.1x below 2.5x target (85% fixed-rate, 7.2-year maturity). 20% or $560 million growth: $300 million spectrum (CBRS/mmWave), $150 million media tuck-ins like regional sports, $110 million R&D AI slicing/NVIDIA recs boosting retention 8%. 5% or $140 million cash build to $8.5 billion.

Our hybrid model (45% wireless, 35% broadband, 20% media) eyes 14% FCF margins by FY2025, like Comcast, virtualizing 40% core with Ericsson dual-mode 5G slashing opex $200 million/year, edge deals for $500 million MEC run-rate 2026. Q3 guide $2.9-3.1 billion, FY2024 $11.8-12.2 billion for dividends/buybacks/content/spectrum.

On capital expenditures, we reaffirm FY2024 at $16.8-17.2 billion or 14% revenue, with 62% or $10.4-10.6 billion to networks—slight uptick for faster 5G Advanced/fiber, offset by supply chain efficiencies.

Wireless: $6.2-6.4 billion (60%), for 25,000 small cells/massive MIMO on C-band/mmWave covering 95% top 100 metros at 450 Mbps. NA 70%, FWA to 2 million homes bundled with GlobalStream—er, NovaStream. Europe $1.1 billion Open RAN with Nokia/Ericsson cutting opex 15%; APAC $800 million sub-6 India/Indonesia.

Wireline/fiber: $2.8-3.0 billion up 12%, XGS-PON to 8 million locations from 6.2 million, 25% annual growth for cloud gaming/Epic/8K. US Southeast $1.2 billion BEAD rural; Europe $600 million GPON UK/Germany; APAC edge DCs.

Media/content: $1.4-1.5 billion (14%), CDN $900 million 200 PoPs AV1 for 30% bitrate cut 4K/8K, AI orchestration like Netflix Open Connect for Olympics peaks.

This supports 5G-6G, spectrum efficiency (1.2 bits/Hz), ESG (40% recycled/renewable). 2025 intensity 12-13% as 5G ROI hits 25% higher margins. Mitigate tariffs/domestic ramps with $2.5 billion financing.

For subscriber and revenue guidance, Q3 closed 158.2 million subs up 4.2% YoY: postpaid mobile +1.1 million, broadband +850,000, video/streaming +12% to 42.5 million—11th straight positive quarter.

Q4: 1.8-2.2 million net adds (1.1-1.4% growth). Mobile +900k-1.1m on 95% 5G Ultra/iPhone 16; broadband +650k-800k FTTH 55 markets/25 million passings; video +250k-300k Disney/ESPN+/Hulu bundles, 1.1% churn AI edge.

FY2025: 7-9% growth, 11-14 million adds to ~170 million (65% 5G mobile, 40% fiber pen). NA 6-8%, Europe 4-6% Vodafone JV, APAC/LATAM 15-18% Brazil/India.

Revenue Q3 $15.2 billion up 6.8%: wireless +5.2%, broadband +9.1%, media +14.3%; ARPU +2.1% to $58.40.

Q4: $15.2-15.5 billion (3.5-5.5% QoQ, 6-8% YoY). Wireless $8.1-8.3b +4-6%; broadband $4.6-4.7b +7-9%; media $2.5-2.6b +12-15% CTV ads/NBCU.

FY2025: $62.5-64.0 billion +9-12% over $57.2 billion FY2024. ARPU +3-4% to $60+ bundles; $2.5b capex 50k fiber miles/Open RAN 15% savings; postpaid 72% revenue, FAST/AVOD vs OTT; Sunbelt M&A. Risks FCC/ad softness, diversified 55% services/25% media/20% equip. Mid-teens EBITDA $24-25b, FCF >$12b.

Blended SAC at $428 Q3, down 7% YoY from $461, 3% from Q1 $441—low end $420-450 FY guide, via digital-first.

Mobility (55% subs): postpaid $385 down 9% on 22% app e-comm/ML personalization like Verizon myPlan; prepaid $290 digital TikTok/YouTube Gen Z 3x ROI, $120 device subs vs T-Mobile.

Broadband/fiber $562 up 4% installs, 45% pen $85 ARPU; NE $510 vs Altice/Charter, Fiber+Stream -12% SAC.

Media $112 down 15%, CTV Roku/Fire TV 40% lower CPM, Lionsgate series 25% higher LTV, <2% churn 48-mo payback.

US $415 down 6% YoY; Europe $480 GDPR Vodafone; APAC $320 down 12% USSD/WhatsApp 60% zero-touch.

AI SAC Optimizer 18% pilot cuts; Disney+/Peacock bundles 20% compression YE; LTV payback 14 mo vs 18. Q3 $415-430, FY $425, 200bps margins H2.

On operating expenses, Q3 total $10.0 billion down 7.2% YoY or $320 million better, third straight reduction; T12 OpEx/revenue 62% from 68%, adding $450 million EBITDA (180bps to 35.4%). FY savings $1.8 billion vs $1.5b, EBITDA upper $12.5-13b.

Targeted: Network (45%)—Open RAN/5G SA 85% US/65% Europe, SDN/NFV AI maintenance 4,200 sites -22% downtime/-35% dispatches $180m ann; copper consol $120m NA; vendor Ericsson/Nokia $50m APAC. Content (25%)—renegotiate 40% rights $250m, bundles 15% uptake revenue-share -28% cash, EMEA shoppable CTV $40m. SG&A (20%)—GenAI chatbot 60% Tier1 care -8% headcount, ZBB $110m cloud ERP. Marketing (10%)—1st-party data CAC $320 -22%, programmatic $90m.

Efficiency Engine top quartile PwC; $500m 2024 edge/6G. Q3 $450m upside, 38%+ margins 2025 > peers, $3b buybacks.

Debt: gross $48.2b ($12b RCF undrawn, $18b term, $18.2b notes); net $45.1b post $3.1b cash; 3.2x LTM EBITDA $14.1b (down 60bps from 3.8x YE23, 1t from 4.3x peak).

EBITDA +12% YoY: wireless +4% 112m postpaid ARPU +2.8% 5G/streaming; broadband +15% 55% US FTx; StreamGlobal 28m subs +22% NFL/AI churn -150bps 4.2%.

US 2.9x FCF $4.2b +18% 5G SA $6.8b Open RAN Nokia/Rakuten. Europe 3.7x EuroLink Spain Digi-like $450m savings 450MHz/42% FTTH. APAC <2.5x India JV 250m 5G +18% tariffs.

Glide 2.5-3.0x 2025 vs Verizon 3.4x/T-Mobile 2.7x/Comcast 2.9x: 50% FCF $5-6b paydown ($1.2b Term B Q3 4.1%); refi $4b 4.75-5.25% maturity 7.2y no 2028 cliffs; towers $2.1b AMT, CBS licensing; 25% covenant excess 3.8x FCC. Q4 capex $1.6b 90% 5G SA AI slicing; interest $1.9b flat $10b swaps 65%.

Fortress BS for regs/5G-media, $3.2b buybacks 45% payout.

David Patel: Thank you. I'd like to provide an update on our network performance. We've made significant strides in expanding our 5G coverage and increasing network capacity. We're also investing in advanced technologies like network slicing and edge computing to support new applications and services. Our network uptime and reliability remain high at 99.99%. We are also improving latency and energy efficiency through AI optimizations and renewable site powering.

Lisa Wong: Thank you. We've seen strong customer growth and improved customer satisfaction scores this quarter to 78 on NPS. Our bundled service offerings are resonating well with customers, and we're focused on providing a seamless and personalized customer experience. We are also focused on increasing ARPU through premium bundles and reducing churn with predictive analytics.

Raj Singh: Thank you. From a technology perspective, we are focused on driving innovation and leveraging emerging technologies to enhance our network and services. We are exploring the use of AI and machine learning to automate network operations and improve efficiency. We are also working on developing new products and services that leverage 5G and edge computing. Our R&D efforts are concentrated on AI-driven personalization and 6G precursors like terahertz trials.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you provide more details on your plans for expanding your presence in the enterprise market and how you plan to compete with existing players, specifically regarding 5G private networks and edge services?

Lisa Wong: Thanks, John. We're aggressively targeting enterprise with tailored 5G private networks and edge slices, building on our Q3 pilots that added key media production wins. Partnerships like Nokia Open RAN enable customized low-latency for AR/VR and IoT, competing head-on by undercutting TCO 25% while bundling NovaStream for Hollywood. We've secured Fortune 500 manufacturing deals for URLLC, projecting $500 million run-rate by 2026, with coverage expanding via 25,000 new small cells.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Carter with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter: Hi, thanks for taking my question. What are your expectations for the impact of inflation and rising interest rates on your business, and how do you plan to mitigate those risks, especially regarding capex and debt management?

Maria Chen: Thanks, Emily. Inflation and rates are headwinds, but our FCF strength and fixed-rate debt (85% at 4.1% blended) buffer us—interest flat YoY despite debt. Capex efficiencies from Open RAN and supply chain hedges offset 8% civil costs; we've prepaid $1.2 billion debt this quarter, targeting 2.5x leverage. OpEx savings $1.8 billion FY and vendor financing $2.5 billion mitigate, keeping EPS mid-teens growth.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mike Rodriguez with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mike Rodriguez: Can you discuss your sustainability initiatives and your plans for reducing your carbon footprint, and how will you measure your success, specifically addressing energy efficiency in network deployments?

Alex Rivera: Thanks, Mike. Sustainability is core—40% new sites renewable/recycled materials, aligning ESG with CalPERS/BlackRock. AI predictive maintenance cut energy 22% at 4,200 sites; we're tracking Scope 1/2 emissions down 15% YoY, targeting net-zero 2035 via 5G SA efficiencies (25% better than 4G). Success metrics: 30% renewable power 2025, reported in annual ESG with third-party audits.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you for your questions. That concludes our Q&A session. Alex, would you like to provide closing remarks?

Alex Rivera: Thank you. In closing, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders. We are committed to innovation, customer satisfaction, and sustainable growth. Thank you for your time and interest in NovaTel Communications Inc.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
